rows.text: Benzene's three laboratory routes span three logics: soda-lime decarboxylation deletes a carboxylate (C₆H₅COONa + NaOH/CaO → C₆H₆ + Na₂CO₃), zinc-dust reduction deletes an oxygen (C₆H₅OH + Zn → C₆H₆ + ZnO), and Berthelot's red-hot trimerisation builds the ring from three ethynes (3C₂H₂, Fe tube, 873 K).…

rows.label: Conditions

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Phenol to benzene and benzene to phenol are the same C-O bond viewed from opposite directions.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Berthelot's synthesis*** - three ethyne molecules cyclise into the aromatic sextet; the stored triple-bond energy and the aromatic stabilisation both push the reaction downhill.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Making Benzene: Three Named Routes The syllabus names three laboratory preparations of benzene: **decarboxylation of sodium benzoate with soda lime**, **distillation of phenol with zinc dust**, and **trimerisation of ethyne through a red-hot iron tube**. Each is a one-line equation with one non-negotiable condition — the conditions are the marks.  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Decarboxylation:** C₆H₅COONa + NaOH(CaO, heat) → C₆H₆ + Na₂CO₃ — soda lime (NaOH + CaO) decarboxylates the salt; the ring carbon keeps its hydrogen. - **From phenol:** C₆H₅OH + Zn (heat) → C₆H₆ + ZnO — zinc dust reduces the C–O bond; distillation drives the benzene over. - **From ethyne:** 3C₂H₂ →(red-hot Fe tube, ~873 K) C₆H₆ — three alkynes cyclise; the reaction is Berthelot's synthesis.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Write the condition over the arrow, always - heat, soda lime, Zn, red-hot Fe tube are arrow labels, not afterthoughts.

rows.text: An equation without its condition is half an answer - the condition is where the mark lives.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Three routes: (1) C6H5COONa + NaOH(CaO, heat) -> C6H6 + Na2CO3 - soda-lime decarboxylation; (2) C6H5OH + Zn(heat) -> C6H6 + ZnO - zinc-dust reduction; (3) 3C2H2 -> (red-hot Fe tube, ~873 K) C6H6 - trimerisation.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Decarboxylation generalises: any sodium benzoate derivative gives the corresponding substituted benzene.
